description: Comprehensive question bank derived from Medieval Indian History FDA & SDA Competitive Examination Notes. Covers Delhi Sultanate, Mughal Empire, Marathas, Bhakti Movement, Sufi Movement, Vijayanagara Empire, Bahmani Sultanate, and Deccan Kingdoms.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What does the term 'Delhi Sultanate' refer to?

options.A: A single dynasty that ruled Delhi
options.B: A series of five dynasties that ruled large parts of northern India from 1206 to 1526 CE
options.D: The British colonial administration in Delhi

questions.explanation: The Delhi Sultanate refers to a series of five dynasties that ruled large parts of northern India from 1206 to 1526 CE, with Delhi as their principal political centre.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which five dynasties ruled the Delhi Sultanate?

options.A: Mamluk, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi

questions.explanation: The five dynasties were the Mamluk or Slave dynasty (1206-1290), Khalji dynasty (1290-1320), Tughlaq dynasty (1320-1414), Sayyid dynasty (1414-1451) and Lodi dynasty (1451-1526).
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who founded the Mamluk or Slave dynasty in India?

options.A: Iltutmish

questions.explanation: Qutb al-Din Aibak founded the Mamluk dynasty in 1206 after the death of Muhammad of Ghor.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What does the term 'Mamluk' mean?

options.A: A hereditary noble
options.B: A military slave or freed military slave who rose to power

questions.explanation: The term Mamluk refers to a military slave or freed military slave who rose to power.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was Qutb al-Din Aibak?

options.A: The first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate who served Muhammad of Ghor as a military commander
options.B: The founder of the Khalji dynasty
options.C: The last ruler of the Mamluk dynasty

questions.explanation: Qutb al-Din Aibak was the first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. He had served Muhammad of Ghor as a military commander and governed the Indian territories before establishing independent rule in 1206.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Why was Qutb al-Din Aibak called 'Lakh Baksh'?

options.A: He conquered lakhs of territories
options.B: He was known for his reputation for generosity

questions.explanation: He was popularly called Lakh Baksh, meaning 'giver of lakhs', because of his reputation for generosity.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which monument was begun by Qutb al-Din Aibak?

options.A: Taj Mahal

questions.explanation: Qutb al-Din Aibak began the construction of the Qutb Minar at Delhi and the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque. The minar was completed and extended by later rulers, especially Iltutmish and Firoz Shah Tughlaq.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who briefly succeeded Qutb al-Din Aibak?

options.A: Iltutmish

questions.explanation: Aram Shah briefly succeeded Aibak, but Iltutmish defeated him and became Sultan in 1211.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who is regarded as the real consolidator of the Delhi Sultanate?

options.A: Qutb al-Din Aibak

questions.explanation: Shams al-Din Iltutmish is generally regarded as the real consolidator of the Delhi Sultanate because he secured Delhi's authority, defeated rivals and strengthened its institutions.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which currency system did Iltutmish introduce or standardise?

options.A: Gold dinar and silver dirham

questions.explanation: Iltutmish introduced or standardised the silver tanka and copper jital currency.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the Chahalgani?

options.A: A group of forty powerful Turkish nobles organised under Iltutmish
options.C: A military unit of forty thousand soldiers

questions.explanation: The Chahalgani, or group of Forty, was a powerful corps of Turkish nobles organised under Iltutmish. Its members later influenced succession and court politics.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was the first woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate?

options.A: Nur Jahan

questions.explanation: Razia Sultan, daughter of Iltutmish, ruled from 1236 to 1240. She is commonly described as the first and only woman to sit on the throne of Delhi as Sultan in her own right.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Why did Razia Sultan face opposition?

options.A: She was not a competent ruler
options.B: Powerful Turkish nobles resisted her independent authority and her appointment of officials outside their preferred elite circle

questions.explanation: Razia faced opposition from powerful Turkish nobles who resisted her independent authority and her appointment of officials outside their preferred elite circle. Court rivalries and regional rebellions contributed to her fall.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When did Balban rule?
questions.explanation: Ghiyas al-Din Balban ruled from 1266 to 1287 and strengthened royal authority through strict court discipline, military organisation and suppression of rebellions.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was Balban's theory of kingship?

options.A: Kingship should be democratic and elected
options.B: He emphasised the exalted and divinely sanctioned status of kingship, strict court etiquette and the ruler's duty to maintain order
options.C: The king should be a religious leader only
options.D: Kingship should be hereditary without any divine connection

questions.explanation: Balban emphasised the exalted and divinely sanctioned status of kingship, strict court etiquette and the ruler's duty to maintain order. He used Persian court practices to enhance royal prestige.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the 'policy of blood and iron' associated with Balban?

options.A: A policy of building iron monuments
options.B: His harsh suppression of rebellions, banditry and threats to the Sultanate
options.C: A policy of trade and commerce

questions.explanation: Balban's policy of 'blood and iron' refers to his harsh suppression of rebellions, banditry and threats to the Sultanate, especially in the Ganga-Yamuna region and frontier areas.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who founded the Khalji dynasty?

options.A: Alauddin Khalji

questions.explanation: Jalal al-Din Firuz Khalji founded the Khalji dynasty in 1290, ending Mamluk rule.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When did Alauddin Khalji rule?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji ruled from 1296 to 1316. He expanded the Sultanate, repelled repeated Mongol attacks, conquered territories in northern and central India and launched campaigns into the Deccan.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which territories were conquered by Alauddin Khalji's forces?

options.A: Gujarat, Ranthambore, Chittor and Malwa
options.D: Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh

questions.explanation: His forces conquered Gujarat, Ranthambore, Chittor and Malwa, and Malik Kafur led expeditions into the Deccan and southern India, including Devagiri, Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was Malik Kafur?

options.A: A general and trusted commander of Alauddin Khalji who led major campaigns into the Deccan and southern India
options.B: The founder of the Tughlaq dynasty
options.C: A Sufi saint of the Chishti order
options.D: The last ruler of the Khalji dynasty

questions.explanation: Malik Kafur was a general and trusted commander of Alauddin Khalji who led major campaigns into the Deccan and southern India in the early fourteenth century.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What were Alauddin Khalji's market reforms?

options.A: He abolished all markets
options.B: He introduced strict price controls for essential commodities and maintained market supervision through officials such as the Shahna-i-Mandi
options.C: He established free trade with foreign countries
options.D: He banned the sale of horses

questions.explanation: Alauddin introduced strict price controls for essential commodities and maintained market supervision through officials such as the Shahna-i-Mandi. He sought to supply his large army at controlled costs.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the 'dagh' system introduced by Alauddin Khalji?

options.A: A system of land measurement
options.B: The branding of horses to prevent substitution of inferior horses

questions.explanation: The dagh system was the branding of horses to prevent the substitution of inferior horses in the Sultan's cavalry.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the 'chehra' system introduced by Alauddin Khalji?

options.A: A system of face reading
options.B: Maintaining descriptive records of soldiers to check personnel and reduce false masters

questions.explanation: The chehra system involved maintaining descriptive records of soldiers so that the army's personnel could be checked and false masters reduced.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What were the main features of Alauddin Khalji's revenue reforms?

options.A: He abolished all taxes
options.B: He strengthened state assessment and collection in the Doab, reduced the power of intermediaries, imposed land revenue at a high proportion, and levied grazing and house taxes
options.C: He introduced a single tax on all citizens
options.D: He exempted all farmers from taxation

questions.explanation: He strengthened state assessment and collection in the Doab, sought to reduce the power of intermediaries, imposed land revenue at a high proportion of assessed produce in some areas, and levied taxes such as grazing and house taxes. Details varied by region.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who seized power after Alauddin Khalji's death?

options.A: Qutb al-Din Mubarak Shah briefly ruled before Khusrau Khan seized power

questions.explanation: After Alauddin's death, a succession struggle followed. Qutb al-Din Mubarak Shah briefly ruled before Khusrau Khan seized power and was defeated by Ghiyas al-Din Tughlaq.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who founded the Tughlaq dynasty?

options.A: Muhammad bin Tughlaq

questions.explanation: Ghiyas al-Din Tughlaq founded the Tughlaq dynasty in 1320 after defeating Khusrau Khan.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When did Muhammad bin Tughlaq rule?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq ruled from 1325 to 1351. He was known for ambitious administrative experiments, intellectual interests and campaigns, several of which faced serious practical difficulties.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Why did Muhammad bin Tughlaq transfer the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad?

options.A: To escape Mongol attacks
options.B: He sought a more centrally located capital and greater control over the Deccan
options.D: To promote trade with southern kingdoms

questions.explanation: He sought a more centrally located capital and greater control over the Deccan. The relocation involved a large movement of people and caused hardship; the court later returned to Delhi. The policy's exact motives are debated.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the token currency experiment of Muhammad bin Tughlaq?

options.A: He introduced gold coins
options.B: He introduced copper or brass token coins intended to circulate at the value of silver currency

questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced copper or brass token coins intended to circulate at the value of silver currency. Counterfeiting and weak control over minting undermined the experiment, and the tokens were withdrawn.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Why did Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduce token currency?

options.A: To simplify trade with foreign countries
options.B: The measure was intended to address the shortage of precious-metal currency and support state finances
options.C: To reduce the power of nobles
options.D: To promote the use of copper in daily life

questions.explanation: The measure was intended to address the shortage of precious-metal currency and support state finances, but its implementation lacked effective safeguards against forgery.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the Doab tax experiment of Muhammad bin Tughlaq?

options.A: He reduced taxes in the Doab region
options.B: He increased taxation in the fertile Ganga-Yamuna Doab, reportedly at a time of crop distress
options.C: He abolished taxes in the Doab region
options.D: He introduced a new tax on trade in the Doab

questions.explanation: He increased taxation in the fertile Ganga-Yamuna Doab, reportedly at a time of crop distress. The measure contributed to peasant hardship and rebellion, although famine and administrative failures were also important.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which traveller visited India during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign?

options.A: Marco Polo

questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta, the Moroccan traveller, visited India and served as a qazi under Muhammad bin Tughlaq. His travel account, the Rihla, is a major source for the period.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who founded the city of Tughlaqabad?

options.A: Muhammad bin Tughlaq

questions.explanation: Ghiyas al-Din Tughlaq founded Tughlaqabad near Delhi and built its fortified city and citadel.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When did Firoz Shah Tughlaq rule?
questions.explanation: Firoz Shah Tughlaq ruled from 1351 to 1388. He undertook public works, canals, gardens, hospitals and educational institutions and sought to stabilise the Sultanate.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What public works are associated with Firoz Shah Tughlaq?

options.A: He built the Taj Mahal
options.B: He repaired and constructed canals, wells, tanks, bridges, gardens, mosques, madrasas and hospitals, and established Firozabad near Delhi

questions.explanation: He repaired and constructed canals, wells, tanks, bridges, gardens, mosques, madrasas and hospitals. He also established the city of Firozabad near Delhi.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was Firoz Shah Tughlaq's policy toward taxation?

options.A: He abolished all taxes
options.B: He sought to organise taxation according to categories recognised by Islamic jurisprudence, including kharaj, jizya, zakat and khums
options.C: He introduced a single tax on all citizens
options.D: He exempted all non-Muslims from taxation

questions.explanation: He sought to organise taxation according to categories recognised by Islamic jurisprudence, including kharaj, jizya, zakat and khums, and is associated with imposing jizya more systematically, including on Brahmanas.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was jizya?

options.A: A tax on agricultural produce
options.B: A tax historically levied by certain Muslim states on specified non-Muslim subjects in return for state protection and exemption from military service
options.C: A tax on trade and commerce

questions.explanation: Jizya was a tax historically levied by certain Muslim states on specified non-Muslim subjects in return for state protection and exemption from military service, though its practice and scope varied by ruler and period.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who invaded Delhi in 1398?

options.A: Babur

questions.explanation: Timur, the Central Asian conqueror, invaded and sacked Delhi in 1398, severely weakening the already fragmented Tughlaq Sultanate.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who founded the Sayyid dynasty?

options.A: Bahlul Lodi

questions.explanation: Khizr Khan founded the Sayyid dynasty in 1414 after taking control of Delhi following Timur's invasion. The dynasty ruled until 1451.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: The Lodi dynasty was of which origin?

options.A: Turkish

questions.explanation: The Lodi were of Afghan origin and were the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When did Sikandar Lodi rule?
questions.explanation: Sikandar Lodi ruled from 1489 to 1517, expanded and strengthened the Lodi kingdom, founded or developed Agra as a major administrative centre in 1504 and promoted agriculture and trade.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which city did Sikandar Lodi develop as a major administrative centre in 1504?

options.A: Delhi

questions.explanation: Sikandar Lodi founded or developed Agra as a major administrative centre in 1504 and promoted agriculture and trade.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was the last Sultan of Delhi from the Lodi dynasty?

options.A: Bahlul Lodi

questions.explanation: Ibrahim Lodi was the last Sultan of Delhi, ruling from 1517 to 1526. He was defeated by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When was the First Battle of Panipat fought?

options.A: 21 April 1526

questions.explanation: The First Battle of Panipat was fought on 21 April 1526 between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi. Babur's victory ended the Lodi dynasty and began Mughal rule in northern India.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the iqta system?

options.A: A system of land ownership by peasants
options.B: A system that assigned revenue rights from specified territories to officials or military commanders in lieu of salary or for administrative and military obligations

questions.explanation: The iqta system assigned revenue rights from specified territories to officials or military commanders in lieu of salary or for administrative and military obligations. An iqtadar or muqtil collected revenue and maintained troops, subject to central supervision.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the role of the ulema in the Delhi Sultanate?

options.A: They were military commanders
options.B: They were Muslim religious scholars and jurists who interpreted Islamic law and could influence religious policy and court affairs

questions.explanation: The ulema were Muslim religious scholars and jurists who interpreted Islamic law and could influence religious policy and court affairs. Their influence varied across rulers.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the principal language of administration and high culture in the Delhi Sultanate?

options.A: Arabic

questions.explanation: Persian was the principal language of the court, administration and much elite literature, although local languages continued to develop and be used in society.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which of the following is an important architectural contribution of the Delhi Sultanate?

options.A: Taj Mahal
options.B: Qutub Minar complex, Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, Alai Darwaza, Tughlaqabad Fort, Firoz Shah Kotla

questions.explanation: Important examples include the Qutub Minar complex, Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, Alai Darwaza, Tughlaqabad Fort, Firoz Shah Kotla and the tombs and mosques of the Lodi period.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the significance of the Mongol threat to the Delhi Sultanate?

options.A: It had no impact on the Sultanate
options.B: Repeated Mongol incursions from the north-west shaped Sultanate military policy, frontier defence and centralisation, especially under Alauddin Khalji
options.C: It led to the immediate collapse of the Sultanate
options.D: It resulted in the establishment of the Mughal Empire

questions.explanation: Repeated Mongol incursions from the north-west shaped Sultanate military policy, frontier defence and centralisation, especially under Alauddin Khalji.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When was the Mughal Empire founded in India?
questions.explanation: The Mughal Empire was founded in 1526 after Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who founded the Mughal Empire in India?

options.A: Akbar

questions.explanation: Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur founded the Mughal Empire in India. He was a descendant of Timur on his father's side and Chinggis Khan through his maternal lineage, according to the dynastic genealogies.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When did Babur live?
questions.explanation: Babur (1483-1530) was a Central Asian ruler from Ferghana who captured Kabul in 1504 and established Mughal rule in northern India after his victory at Panipat in 1526.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which book is Babur's autobiography?

options.A: Akbarnama

questions.explanation: Baburnama, also called Tuzuk-i-Baburi, is Babur's memoir, originally written in Chagatai Turkish. It describes his life, campaigns, geography, people, plants and animals.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: In which language was the Baburnama originally written?

options.A: Persian

questions.explanation: Baburnama is Babur's memoir, originally written in Chagatai Turkish. It describes his life, campaigns, geography, people, plants and animals.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which battles consolidated Babur's rule in India?

options.A: First Battle of Panipat (1526), Battle of Khanwa (1527), Battle of Chanderi (1528), Battle of Ghaghra (1529)
options.B: Battle of Talikota (1565), Battle of Panipat (1761)
options.C: Battle of Plassey (1757), Battle of Buxar (1764)
options.D: Second Battle of Panipat (1556), Battle of Haldighati (1576)

questions.explanation: Babur's key victories included the First Battle of Panipat (1526), the Battle of Khanwa (1527) against Rana Sanga, the Battle of Chanderi (1528) and the Battle of Ghaghra (1529).
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the Battle of Khanwa?

options.A: A battle between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi
options.B: A battle fought in 1527 between Babur and the Rajput confederacy led by Rana Sanga
options.C: A battle between Akbar and Hemu
options.D: A battle between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Durrani

questions.explanation: The Battle of Khanwa was fought in 1527 between Babur and the Rajput confederacy led by Rana Sanga. Babur's victory strengthened his position in northern India.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who succeeded Babur?

options.A: Akbar

questions.explanation: Babur was succeeded by his son Humayun in 1530.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who defeated Humayun and established the Sur Empire?

options.A: Babur

questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun and established the Sur dynasty, ruling much of northern India from 1540 to 1545.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What were Sher Shah Suri's administrative reforms?

options.A: He abolished all taxes
options.B: He reorganised land revenue assessment, improved roads and communications, strengthened policing and administration, and standardised currency including the silver rupiya

questions.explanation: Sher Shah reorganised land revenue assessment, improved roads and communications, strengthened policing and administration, and standardised currency, including the silver rupiya.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which road was greatly improved by Sher Shah Suri?

options.A: Silk Road

questions.explanation: Sher Shah improved the major route later known as the Grand Trunk Road, connecting Bengal with northern India and extending toward the north-west.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was Sher Shah Suri's silver rupiya?

options.A: A gold coin
options.B: A standardised silver coin that was an important precursor to the later rupee currency system

questions.explanation: Sher Shah standardised a silver coin called the rupiya, an important precursor to the later rupee currency system.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who succeeded Sher Shah Suri?

options.A: Humayun

questions.explanation: Sher Shah was succeeded by his son Islam Shah Suri. The Sur Empire later weakened amid succession struggles.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When did Humayun regain Delhi?
questions.explanation: Humayun regained Delhi in 1555 after defeating the Sur forces, but he died in 1556 following a fall on the stairs of his library at Delhi.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who succeeded Humayun?

options.A: Babur

questions.explanation: His son Akbar succeeded him in 1556, initially under the regency of Bairam Khan.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When did Akbar rule?
questions.explanation: Akbar ruled from 1556 to 1605 and greatly expanded and consolidated the Mughal Empire.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When was the Second Battle of Panipat fought?

options.A: 21 April 1526

questions.explanation: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought on 5 November 1556 between Akbar's forces under Bairam Khan and the forces of Hemu. The Mughal victory secured Akbar's position in northern India.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was Bairam Khan?

options.A: Akbar's guardian, regent and leading military commander during the early years of his reign
options.B: The founder of the Sur dynasty

questions.explanation: Bairam Khan was Akbar's guardian, regent and leading military commander during the early years of Akbar's reign. Akbar dismissed him in 1560.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was Akbar's policy of 'sulh-i-kul'?

options.A: A policy of military conquest
options.B: A policy of universal peace and religious tolerance that included people of different religious backgrounds in imperial service

questions.explanation: Akbar pursued a policy often described as sulh-i-kul, or universal peace, and included people of different religious backgrounds in imperial service. He abolished the pilgrimage tax in 1563 and jizya in 1564.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When did Akbar abolish the pilgrimage tax and jizya?

options.A: Pilgrimage tax in 1563 and jizya in 1564
options.B: Pilgrimage tax in 1564 and jizya in 1563

questions.explanation: Akbar abolished the pilgrimage tax in 1563 and jizya in 1564 as part of his policy of religious tolerance.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the Ibadat Khana?

options.A: A military barracks
options.B: A hall of religious discussion established by Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575

questions.explanation: The Ibadat Khana was a hall of religious discussion established by Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575, where scholars and representatives of different religious traditions debated.
questions.source: 6.2 Medieval Indian History - FDA & SDA Notes

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was Din-i Ilahi?

questions.question: What was the jagirdari system?

options.B: He was the founder of the Bahmani Sultanate

questions.explanation: Mahmud Gawan was a Persian-born statesman and chief minister of the Bahmani Sultanate during the fifteenth century.
